title: How git helps with broken code

choices.a: Correct. Each commit records the state of all the project's files at that moment. You can see what changed since the version that worked, and you can go back to that version.
choices.b: Wrong. The .git folder holds git's record of every version. It does not lock your files; you edit them normally.
choices.c: Wrong. This describes GitHub, a website that stores copies of git repos online. Git itself is a program that runs on your computer and works offline.
choices.d: Wrong. Git does not find or fix bugs. It records versions, so you can compare them and go back to an earlier one.
